label: prf:q-gl-obstruction-calc
title: Proof of the obstruction to $q$-flatness
html:
Item (1). The q-flatness equation is \nabla_q^2 = (q-1)\mathcal{F}_q (q-flat connection). Its intrinsic part \mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{intr}} is a class in HH^2(\mathcal{U}_q, \mathrm{Ad}). HKR alone relates polyvector fields to Hochschild cohomology; it does not identify HH^2(\mathcal{U}_q, \mathrm{Ad}) with H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m). That identification is hypothesis (H-HKR), under which \Theta(\mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{intr}}) = \kappa_0 = e(\xi) (Kummer filtration). Since \Theta is injective, \mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{intr}} \neq 0 whenever \kappa_0 \neq 0.

Item (2). q-flatness is the vanishing of the connection-dependent part \mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{conn}}, while \kappa_0 determines the intrinsic part \mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{intr}} (item 1). The two are separate, so \kappa_0 \neq 0 does not prevent q-flatness; it only makes the intrinsic curvature non-zero. The lifting requirement is the quantum lifting condition: lifting from level n needs \kappa_n = 0, and \kappa_n \equiv \kappa_0 \pmod n, which gives \kappa_0 \in n\,H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m).

Item (3). By (H-tr), \mathrm{tr} induces an isomorphism H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m)/n \cong \mathbb{Z}/n sending \kappa_0 \bmod n to \chi(A) \bmod n. So \kappa_0 \bmod n = 0 if and only if n \mid \chi(A). Without (H-tr) the trace alone would not determine the class. The complementary subgroup structure \kappa_n = \kappa_0 + \delta_n prevents cancellation.

Item (4). The set \{n : n \mid \chi(A)\} has exactly d(|\chi(A)|) elements, where d is the divisor function. This set is finite. Its complement in \mathbb{Z}_{>0} has density 1. \square
